verdict.rationale: CDP documents deposit destinations: stable onchain addresses that customers or external parties send funds to, with each deposit automatically credited to the corresponding account's balance. That gives address-to-account attribution. The docs do not explicitly say you can issue one address per end customer, attach customer labels or metadata, or offer named fiat virtual accounts. missing for 10: explicit per-customer address provisioning, customer metadata or labels on destinations, named fiat virtual accounts, reconciliation detail in deposit events, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, incoming funds are attributable — named virtual accounts or dedicated deposit addresses per customer so reconciliation knows who paid without manual matching

citations.quote: Deposit destinations are crypto addresses that your customers or external parties can use to send funds directly. When a deposit arrives, the corresponding account's balance is credited automatically.
Provision stable onchain addresses that auto-credit a custodial account
